column1: # The Belarusian alphabet, one letter per row. This is the ONE place this project's
# word-character class and case-fold table are written down. Do not derive either from
# Unicode's general \p{Cyrillic} property or from str.lower()/str.upper(): both are
# src/pravapis/tokenize.py's BELARUSIAN_LETTERS is the `lower` column; its uppercase
# counterpart set (used to build the tokenizer's word-character regex) is `upper`.
# scripts/check_charclass_sync.py fails CI if either drifts from this file.
# ґ is Taraškievica-only (Narkamaŭka never produces it — see data/NORMS.md, "Project
# decision: no ґ") but must still be recognised as a word character when it appears in
# input, so it is listed here rather than only in a rules table.
